name: Upma
cuisine: South Indian (Karnataka/Tamil Nadu "rava upma"), also a Mumbai Udupi-café and Maharashtrian home staple (where a turmeric version is called "sanja")

ingredients.name: Groundnut oil (or any neutral cooking oil)
Ghee
ingredients.householdMeasure: ½ tsp (optional, for aroma at the end)

ingredients.name: Ginger (adrak)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ½ inch piece, finely chopped (1 tsp)

ingredients.name: Onion (pyaz/kanda)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ½ small onion, finely chopped (about ⅓ cup)

equipment: Kadai or heavy-bottomed pan with a lid
Small plate or bowl to hold the roasted rava
Small saucepan or electric kettle to boil the water
Measuring cup and spoons (a regular tea cup and teaspoons work as a stand-in)

steps.title: Measure the rava
steps.text: Put 50 g (⅓ cup) semolina into a small bowl.
steps.visualCue: Dry, free-flowing granules with no insects or lumps.
steps.cameraCheck: ⅓ cup rava in the bowl
steps.videoShot: Rava pouring from the cup into the bowl.

steps.title: Dry-roast the rava
steps.text: Put the kadai on medium-low heat, add the rava with no oil, and stir continuously.
steps.tip: Keep stirring. If you see brown specks, take the pan off the heat at once.
steps.visualCue: The granules look drier and flow like sand, turn a shade paler cream (not brown), and smell lightly toasted.
steps.cameraCheck: The roasted rava in the pan
steps.videoShot: The spatula moving the rava in slow circles.

steps.title: Move the rava out
steps.text: Tip the roasted rava onto a plate and spread it out so it stops cooking.
steps.visualCue: A thin, even layer on the plate

steps.title: Chop the onion
steps.text: Finely chop 50 g (½ small) onion.
steps.visualCue: Small, even pieces about the size of a lentil
steps.cameraCheck: ⅓ cup chopped onion on the board

steps.title: Dice the carrot
steps.text: Peel and finely dice 20 g carrot.
steps.visualCue: Small cubes about the size of a pea, so they cook in 2–3 min

steps.title: Chop the ginger
steps.text: Peel and finely chop a ½ inch piece of ginger (3 g).
steps.visualCue: Tiny bits, no long fibres

steps.title: Slit the chilli
steps.text: Slit 1 green chilli (5 g) lengthwise, or chop it small if you like more heat.
steps.tip: Slit, not chopped, gives flavour with less heat. You can pick it out before eating.
steps.visualCue: Split chilli or small rings

steps.title: Prepare the herbs
steps.text: Wash 6–8 curry leaves and pat them dry. Chop 5 g (1 tbsp) coriander leaves.
steps.visualCue: Curry leaves are dry, so they won't splutter hard.
steps.cameraCheck: Curry leaves and chopped coriander side by side

steps.title: Boil the water
steps.text: Heat 200 ml (¾ cup + 1 tbsp) water in a small pan or kettle.
steps.visualCue: Rolling boil with big bubbles

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Put the kadai back on medium heat and add 10 ml (2 tsp) oil.
steps.visualCue: The oil shimmers and flows easily when you tilt the pan.

steps.title: Add the mustard seeds
steps.text: Add 1 g (¼ tsp) mustard seeds.
steps.visualCue: The seeds crackle and pop.

steps.title: Add the dals
steps.text: Add 3 g (1 tsp) chana dal and 3 g (1 tsp) urad dal and stir.
steps.tip: Take them to light golden only. They darken more once the onion goes in.
steps.visualCue: Both dals turn light golden and smell nutty.

steps.title: Add the cashews
steps.text: Add 3–4 cashew halves (5 g).
steps.visualCue: Cashews turn pale gold at the edges.

steps.title: Add the hing, ginger, chilli and curry leaves
steps.text: Add a pinch of asafoetida, then the ginger, green chilli and curry leaves.
steps.tip: Stand back. Wet leaves splutter hard.
steps.visualCue: A loud splutter, then crisp, glossy leaves and a sharp ginger smell.

steps.title: Sauté the onion
steps.text: Add the chopped onion and stir.
steps.visualCue: The onion is soft and translucent, not brown.
steps.cameraCheck: The soft onions in the pan

steps.title: Cook the vegetables
steps.text: Add the diced carrot and 15 g (1½ tbsp) peas. Stir.
steps.visualCue: The carrot is brighter orange and the peas are bright green.

steps.title: Add the water
steps.text: Pour in the 200 ml boiling water (or cold water, then bring it to a boil here). Add 1.5 g (¼ tsp) salt and 1 g (¼ tsp) sugar, if using.
steps.tip: Taste the water now. It should taste slightly saltier than you want the upma, because the rava will absorb it.
steps.visualCue: Water at a rolling boil over the vegetables
steps.cameraCheck: The boiling water in the kadai
steps.videoShot: Water pouring in and bubbling up.

steps.title: Lower the heat
steps.text: Turn the flame to low.
steps.visualCue: The water is now simmering gently, not splashing.

steps.title: Add the rava
steps.text: Pour the roasted rava into the water in a thin stream with one hand while stirring constantly with the other.
steps.tip: Hot water spits as it thickens. Hold the pan handle with a cloth. If lumps form, press them against the side of the pan.
steps.visualCue: The mixture thickens into a soft, smooth mass with no dry pockets or lumps.
steps.cameraCheck: The thickened upma in the pan
steps.videoShot: Rava streaming in while the spatula stirs.

steps.title: Steam the upma
steps.text: Cover with the lid and cook on the lowest heat.
steps.visualCue: When you open it, the surface looks fluffy and the grains are swollen and soft.
steps.cameraCheck: The covered pan, then the open pan
steps.videoShot: The lid lifting and steam rising.

steps.title: Add the ghee
steps.text: Switch off the heat. Add ½ tsp ghee (optional) and fold it through.
steps.visualCue: A light gloss on the upma
steps.videoShot: The ghee melting, then a fold.

steps.title: Rest the upma
steps.text: Leave it covered off the heat.
steps.visualCue: The upma loosens and separates when you fluff it with the spatula.

steps.title: Add the lemon and coriander
steps.text: Squeeze 5 ml (1 tsp) lemon juice and scatter the chopped coriander. Give one gentle fold.
steps.visualCue: Green flecks over cream-coloured upma, with orange carrot and green peas
steps.cameraCheck: The finished upma in the pan
steps.videoShot: Lemon dripping, coriander falling, one fold.

steps.title: Plate the upma
steps.text: Spoon it onto a plate, or press it into a small bowl and turn it out for a neat mound.
steps.visualCue: Soft, moist and holds its shape lightly, not runny or stiff
steps.videoShot: A slow pan across the finished plate.

reasons: the home version uses 2 tsp oil plus an optional ½ tsp ghee, no deep frying, very little sugar, and adds carrot, peas and onion, with a little extra protein from the dals and cashews. But rava is refined wheat, so the dish is mostly fast-digesting carbohydrate with modest protein (about 11 g) and fibre. Restaurant upma usually has more ghee or oil, a heavier hand with salt, fewer vegetables, and often a sev or fried-cashew topping.

researchRating.basis: upma is a well-loved, everyday South Indian and Mumbai breakfast. Recipe pages score highly (snippets showed ratings from 4.34 to 5 stars, including 4.86 from 54 votes), and Matunga cafés such as Sharda Bhavan and Mani's are praised for it. Points are deducted because it is famously polarising: a 2017 Twitter row (over a suggestion that upma be a "national dish") and recurring "boring/sticky upma" jokes show a strong dislike among a large group, mostly because bad versions turn gluey or lumpy.

storage: Can go in the fridge for up to 2 days in an airtight box (it firms up as it cools). Freezing is possible for up to 1 month but the texture turns slightly grainy, so it is not ideal. To reheat, sprinkle 1–2 tbsp water, cover, and warm on low in a pan for 3–4 min, breaking it up with a spatula, or microwave covered for 1 min. Add fresh lemon after reheating.
leftoverRemix: Crispy upma tikkis. Mash cold leftover upma with 1 tbsp besan, 1 tbsp grated cheese or paneer and a pinch of chilli flakes. Shape into small flat patties and shallow-fry on a tawa with 1 tsp oil for about 3 min per side until golden. Serve with green chutney or ketchup.
burnOff: about 5.5 km of running (387 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 7.7 km of brisk walking (about 1 hr 30 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.).
